name: Nuclear plant safety
value: ZNPP off-site power lost and restored 8 Nov
summary: Zaporizhzhia lost all off-site power on 8 Nov for the 27th time; the IAEA said it was restored about 10 hours later
state: Zaporizhzhia lost its sole 330 kV external line on 8 Nov, the 27th total loss of off-site power of the war, and ran on emergency diesel generators until the IAEA confirmed power was restored about 10 hours later (Kyiv Independent, 9 Nov). The cause and location of the fault are not yet known, and Director General Grossi described a continued precarious nuclear safety situation. No damage to safety systems or radiological release was reported.
for_you: There is no radiological risk reported to the public. People in the region should follow guidance from Ukraine's State Nuclear Regulatory Inspectorate; the IAEA publishes updates on the plant.
rubric_hit: Plant lost all off-site power (8 Nov); no damage to safety systems or release

sources.title: Kyiv Independent — Power to Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant cut, restored, IAEA says

why: Fighting near nuclear power plants risks a radiological release; the IAEA reports on Zaporizhzhia and other plants in or near war zones.
drivers: Off-site power losses, strikes near plants, staffing, cooling water, military occupation.

rubric.alert: Damage to safety-critical systems, an INES level 2 or higher event, or a radiological release.
rubric.watch: A plant loses all off-site power, strikes land near a plant, or the IAEA reports a deteriorating safety situation.
rubric.normal: No new IAEA safety concerns at plants in or near conflict zones.
